mapping_note: paper wording 'conditioned responding was attenuated ... as was dopamine neuron activity and dopamine release' -> our K2 inhibition/gate; 'event i is kept in memory ... according to an eligibility trace ... T ... a fraction of the mean inter-reward interval' -> our K5 delay/memory (the reward interval parameterises the memory timescale). The paper never uses 'gate' or 'memory timescale' as family labels.
description_scope: Judged under the description 'a rat's anticipatory head-port entry during the 20-s cue, measured while the cue-reward interval and the average reward rate are held constant and only the outcome-specific contingency is degraded'; the action judgement is made on the contingency description, not on any interval description.
motion_source: L3 physiological carrier: VTA dopamine cell activity (GCaMP6f) and nucleus accumbens dopamine release (dLight1.1) during outcome-selective Pavlovian contingency degradation in rats, plus optogenetic dopamine stimulation/inhibition.

mechanism.claim: Adding noncontingent rewards in the intertrial interval attenuates the conditioned response and the cue- and reward-evoked dopamine signals for that specific contingency only, i.e. the gate on responding closes even though the cue-reward interval is unchanged.
mechanism.quote: Conditioned responding was attenuated for the cue-reward contingency that was degraded, as was dopamine neuron activity in the midbrain and dopamine release in the ventral striatum in response to the cue and subsequent reward.

mechanism.claim: In the ANCCR simulations that best explained the data, the decay time constant of the cue memory trace is parameterised as a free fraction of the mean inter-reward interval, i.e. the reward interval sets the timescale over which the association is held.
mechanism.quote: Event i is kept in memory across time steps according to an eligibility trace E ← i = ∑ t i ≤ t e − ( t − t i T ) (7) where T is the temporal decay parameter. T was always considered a fraction of the mean inter-reward interval during acquisition, and this fraction ( T ratio) was a free parameter used to fit the model.

event_grammar: [MOTION] a noncontingent reward is delivered during the ITI at the same average rate as cued rewards (L3/L0) --> [GATE] the retrospective cue-reward contingency, not the cue-reward interval, falls, so the cue stops signalling a rate change (C/T) (L0) --> [INACTION] anticipatory head entries to the degraded cue are attenuated while responding to the nondegraded cue persists / [ACTION] retained for the intact contingency (L4) --> [OUTCOME] cue- and reward-evoked dopamine lose their phasic control and their trial-by-trial history dependence (L3) --> [FEEDBACK] retrospective (ANCCR) update of the predecessor association with a trace constant tied to the mean inter-reward interval (L0/L3)

anchor_concordance.reason: Neither: it holds the cue-reward interval constant and degrades contingency, so it does not test that the interval sets the learning rate; it extends only the weaker cluster premise that dopamine tracks temporal contingency/reward-rate structure rather than the number of pairings, and it parameterises its trace with the mean inter-reward interval.
